_description: Standing macro/geopolitical situations referenced across briefings. Loader: scripts/generate_daily.py:load_ongoing_situations(). Manually maintained. Set status to 'resolved' when a situation is over, or 'expired' when its facts are out of date; the loader skips both. Each entry carries its own 'updated' date (YYYY-MM-DD); the loader drops an 'active' entry older than STALE_SITUATIONS_DAYS (14) from the prompt and lists it for the fact check. To bring one back, write facts from a dated source, set 'updated' to that date and status to 'active'. Add new situations when they enter the briefing rotation. Keep facts list under 6 items per situation (loader caps at 6). Anchor phrase is the one-clause framing used on FIRST reference each week per Rule 18.

iran_hormuz.anchor: the Iran-Hormuz cycle: a July re-escalation (vessels hit, tankers reversing, crude running) that has since cooled, with the premium deflating again into August
facts: the situation re-escalated in early-to-mid July: commercial vessels hit, tanker traffic reversed course, and crude ran multi-percent sessions on Iran headlines
by late July the market's focus shifted from Hormuz risk to Red Sea/Houthi rerouting costs, two offsetting freight stories
as of Aug 3 the briefing's own read: crude supply building, Hormuz premium still deflating, no input-cost surprise
the premium has built and unwound twice since April; treat fresh escalation headlines as a known pattern, not a new regime
diesel tightness, not crude, has been the input-cost story for fall fieldwork

china_trade_deal.anchor: the US-China trade truce, first struck in Busan on Oct 30, 2025 and now extended to Jan 10, 2027, with China pledged to buy 25 million metric tons of US soybeans a year through 2028
facts: On Sep 24, 2026, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Busan truce, which was set to end Nov 10, 2026, is extended to Jan 10, 2027 (S&P Global, Sep 24, 2026). Never call Nov 10 the deadline.
China agreed to buy 25 million metric tons of US soybeans a year from 2026 through 2028. On Sep 24 Bessent said China has been meeting the soybean commitment.
A separate pledge of $17 billion a year in other US farm and food purchases came out of the May 2026 Trump-Xi meeting in Beijing. On Sep 24 Bessent said China is a little behind on those.

As of the Sep 24 report, USDA data showed China had committed to 9.969 million metric tons of US soybeans so far in the 2026/27 marketing year (Sept-Aug). Newer weekly export sales outrank this number.
US soybeans still pay 13% at China's border (3% MFN plus a 10% added levy); Brazilian soybeans pay 3%.

cargill_fort_morgan_lockout.expired_why: last confirmation on file is end of July. Oct 20 check: a search listing shows a Denver7 headline saying the lockout ended after 88 days with a new five-year contract, but the page is blocked from the sandbox and not on the references branch, so the ending is not confirmed and is not written here.
cargill_fort_morgan_lockout.anchor: the Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19, still removing roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity
facts: 1,700 workers were still locked out as of the end of July, the last confirmation on file. If today's news has an update, prefer it and say so.
Roughly 6,000 head/day of processing capacity remains removed on that last confirmation.
The dynamic is processing-constrained, not supply-constrained: packer margins, not cattle numbers, are the binding constraint.

growing_season_2026.anchor: USDA's Oct 9 crop report, which raised both yields from September: corn 181.2 bu/acre and soybeans 53.1
facts: USDA's Oct 9, 2026 Crop Production and WASDE: corn yield 181.2 bu/acre, up from 178.5 in September; production 16.034 billion bushels on 88.5 million harvested acres (96.8 million planted).
Soybean yield 53.1 bu/acre, up from 52.8 in September; production 4.562 billion bushels on 85.9 million harvested acres (86.9 million planted).
2026/27 ending stocks: corn 1.849 billion bushels (1.567 in September), soybeans 315 million (310), wheat 740 million (717).
Season-average farm price: corn $4.70 (down from $4.80), soybeans $12.00 (unchanged), wheat $6.30 (down from $6.40).
These are USDA's current numbers until the next Crop Production and WASDE on Nov 10, 2026. August's 180.7/52.7 and September's 178.5/52.8 yields are superseded and must never be quoted as current.

cattle_mexico_screwworm.expired_why: the Aug 24 Douglas reopening date has passed. Oct 20 check: search listings show KOLD (Aug 24) reporting Douglas reopened to Mexican cattle that day, but no page could be opened from the sandbox and the references branch holds no APHIS source, so the current border status is not confirmed and is not written here.
cattle_mexico_screwworm.anchor: the screwworm-driven closure of Mexican feeder cattle imports, with the first phased port reopening set for Aug 24 at Douglas, AZ
facts: The border closure has tightened feeder supply all summer and is one leg of the historic feeder rally.
USDA confirmed a phased reopening starting Aug 24 at Douglas, AZ, still UPCOMING as of Aug 15; do not describe ports as reopened.
Feeders broke roughly 3% in late July as the market began pricing returning supply rather than scarcity.
The feeder/live spread is the tell as the Aug 24 date approaches.
Screwworm spread beyond Texas earlier in the season; containment progress drives the reopening pace.

farm_bill_2026.anchor: the 2026 farm bill: the extension of the 2018 law ran out Sep 30, and the House and Senate bills are still not reconciled
facts: The latest extension of the 2018 Farm Bill expired Sep 30, 2026. As of mid-October no new farm bill has passed (Farm Policy News, read Oct 16, 2026). Do not say a new extension passed unless today's news says so.

The Senate Agriculture Committee advanced the Agricultural Act of 2026 on a 12-11 party-line vote in September, after Sen. McConnell returned. It was reported to the Senate as S. 5526 on Sep 24, 2026.
Chairman Boozman said the Senate bill is not expected to get a floor vote before the election. House and Senate members will instead meet informally to work out the differences.
The House passed its bill, the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, 224-200 on Apr 30, 2026, without year-round E15. The Senate bill authorizes year-round E15 sales.
Nothing is law yet: the Senate bill still needs a floor vote, a deal with the House and the president's signature.

_maintenance: Refresh whenever a dated claim inside it passes. An 'active' entry whose 'updated' date (or, without one, this file's _last_updated) is more than STALE_SITUATIONS_DAYS old is dropped from the Daily prompt, not just flagged, and listed in the fact check's log. A stale standing fact outranks current news in the writer's context, which is how a wrong date becomes a published claim. 2026-10-20: china_trade_deal, farm_bill_2026 and growing_season_2026 rewritten from dated pages (each entry's 'source' and 'source_date'); iran_hormuz, cargill_fort_morgan_lockout and cattle_mexico_screwworm stay expired because no page for them could be opened. Active entries now drop out on Nov 3 unless refreshed; growing_season_2026 must be rewritten after the Nov 10 report.
